_comment: arms.config.json — arm -> model configuration (issue #5, pre-registration §3.1). Config, not code: the runner (evals/harness/runner.mjs) READS this file; it never hardcodes a model ID. Panel size is fixed at 5 agents / ideasPerAgent: 6 / maxRounds: 2 for every panel arm (A is the one exception - a single solo call, no panel) so the ONLY thing varying between arms is model assignment, per the pre-registration's design intent ('the only thing varying is model assignment') -- true of arms A through AS. The eight S1-* arms (issue #130, Appendix F item 2) are a SEPARATE one-factor-at-a-time screening design layered on top: each varies exactly one of N / effort / stance / strategy off a centre point (S1-C0), so 'the only thing varying' does not hold across the S1-* family as a whole -- see each S1-* arm's own `purpose` for which single factor it moves.
_modelIdSource: Anthropic model IDs verified against the claude-api skill (cached 2026-06-24) and docs/PREREGISTRATION.md §8.1: claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-haiku-4-5. OpenAI model IDs verified first-party against developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (2026-08-02, issue #22) -- see lib/price.mjs's OPENAI_PRICE_VERIFICATION record; the earlier UNVERIFIED placeholders (openai-mid-tier / openai-large-tier) are removed. Tier-matching judgment (issue #22): the study varies model configuration only, so G's two OpenAI slots sit at tiers comparable to the Anthropic slots they contrast with -- gpt-5.6-terra (mid tier, ~Sonnet-comparable) and gpt-5.6-sol (flagship tier, ~Opus-comparable); H is homogeneous OpenAI at the mid tier (gpt-5.6-terra x5), the OpenAI analogue of arm C (homogeneous Sonnet).

A.label: Solo baseline
A.purpose: The control that can falsify the product -- single call, no panel, no rounds. totalIdeasRequested: 30 (5 x 6, maxRounds: 1) -- this is Arm A's ROUND-1-ONLY total, and Arm A has only one round, so it is Arm A's whole pool. A panel arm is NOT matched to this at pool level: panel.maxRounds is 2, round 2 APPENDS to round 1's candidates rather than replacing them, so a panel arm's real pool is ~60 (size x ideasPerAgent x maxRounds), not 30. See evals/judge/matrix.mjs's judgeLegsFor comment for the pre-flight pricing consequence of this asymmetry.

E.label: Anthropic tiered mix
E.purpose: The 'combination' hypothesis (H2): does heterogeneity buy diversity cheaply? 2xHaiku, 2xSonnet, 1xOpus.

F.label: Anthropic inverted mix
F.purpose: Separates heterogeneity from average capability: E and F differ in tier mix at similar spread. 2xOpus, 3xHaiku.

H.label: Homogeneous OpenAI
H.purpose: Control for G -- isolates 'cross-provider' from 'OpenAI is just different'.

A'.label: Ablation: persona-disabled panel
A'.purpose: Cheap, high-value ablation. Panel of 5 identical models with IDENTICAL personas (persona lever disabled). Isolates how much of the panel's benefit is persona engineering vs. merely sampling 5 times.

AS.label: Solo baseline, stance-neutral control
AS.purpose: issue #129 amendment F. Arm A's slot persona 'solo' is not a DEFAULT_PERSONAS name, so ideate-core falls through to DEFAULT_PERSONAS[0] -- PRAGMATIST, stance-assigned, strategy 'direct' -- which means arm A varies from the panel arms in stance AND strategy AND rounds AND model, all at once. AS aims to isolate the STANCE lever only: personaDisabled (+ uniformPersona) forces the SAME explicit, perspective-free stance arm A' uses for its panel ablation, and uniformPersona overrides temperature/strategy back to PRAGMATIST's assumed values (0.4/direct, verified against ideate-core@0.5.0's DEFAULT_PERSONAS[0] -- not independently re-verified against a live ideate-core call from this harness) instead of taking UNIFORM_PERSONA's cot-leaning defaults, so AS is BUILT to differ from arm A in stance only. Same model (claude-sonnet-5), same totalIdeasRequested (30), same maxRounds (1) as arm A. `uniformPersona.persona` is deliberately inert (no reference to 'stance' or 'neutral' in the string sent to the model, unlike an earlier draft's 'solo_stance_neutral') -- the persona name reaches the model verbatim in the round-1 prompt (evals/harness/prompts.mjs), and naming the experimental construct in the prompt text would be a demand characteristic.

S1-C0.label: Study 1 Stage 1a — centre point
S1-C0.purpose: Appendix F item 2. The centre of the one-factor-at-a-time screening design: N=30, effort high, stance neutral, strategy cot. Every other S1 arm differs from this one in exactly ONE factor, which is what makes the sweep attributable. `effort: high` is documented as behaviourally equivalent to omitting the parameter (Appendix F item 5), so this centre point is also the sweep's bridge to the effort-free arms A and AS.

S1-N10.label: Study 1 Stage 1a — N=10
S1-N10.purpose: Appendix F item 2. Off-centre on N only (10 vs the centre's 30). Feeds the distinct_k-vs-N dose-response curve, which is the study's headline deliverable and the denominator every later panel comparison needs.

S1-N60.label: Study 1 Stage 1a — N=60
S1-N60.purpose: Appendix F item 2. Off-centre on N only (60 vs 30). Appendix F item 7 records a measured risk specific to this arm: 1 of 6 probe replies at N=60 failed a direct JSON.parse and lost 14 objects to salvage while ending on end_turn — malformation, not truncation, so the raised max_tokens cap does not address it. Short realized pools here should be checked against that first.

S1-ELOW.label: Study 1 Stage 1a — effort low
S1-ELOW.purpose: Appendix F item 2. Off-centre on effort only (low vs high). Within-model by construction: Appendix E item 3 registers effort as a first-class ordinal factor ONLY within one model family, because the Anthropic and OpenAI ladders are verified but not identical.

S1-EMAX.label: Study 1 Stage 1a — effort max
S1-EMAX.purpose: Appendix F item 2. Off-centre on effort only (max vs high). This is the arm the effort-aware max_tokens sizing (Appendix F item 6) exists for: measured live at up to 775.6 output tokens per idea, 5.0x the cap the pre-#130 constants would have applied, so under the old sizing it would have truncated systematically and read as a dose-response effect of effort on distinct_k.

S1-SPRAG.label: Study 1 Stage 1a — stance PRAGMATIST
S1-SPRAG.purpose: Appendix F item 2. Off-centre on stance only. The stance string is ideate-core@0.5.0's DEFAULT_PERSONAS[0] text, transcribed VERBATIM — but its bundled strategy ('direct') is deliberately NOT carried over: strategy stays at the centre value 'cot'. That separation is the point of the arm. DEFAULT_PERSONAS ships stance and strategy together, so a persona effect measured on the main grid is un-attributable between perspective and prompt strategy; this arm moves perspective alone.

uniformPersona.stance: PRAGMATIST: practical, resource-aware, shippable. Favor ideas that a small team could start on Monday. Prefer clarity and feasibility over cleverness.

S1-SCONTRA.label: Study 1 Stage 1a — stance CONTRARIAN
S1-SCONTRA.purpose: Appendix F item 2. Off-centre on stance only. DEFAULT_PERSONAS[1]'s stance text verbatim, with its bundled strategy ('cot') coinciding with the centre value rather than being carried over — the same unbundling as S1-SPRAG. The persona NAME stays the inert 'solo_b' on every S1 arm: buildRound1Prompt interpolates the name into the prompt verbatim, so a descriptive name here would leak the manipulation into the text and reintroduce the demand characteristic arm AS's inert name was chosen to remove.

uniformPersona.stance: CONTRARIAN: challenge the obvious. Invert the default assumption, argue the opposite of the expected move, and surface what everyone is ignoring.

S1-DIRECT.label: Study 1 Stage 1a — strategy direct
S1-DIRECT.purpose: Appendix F item 2. Off-centre on strategy only (direct vs the centre's cot). This is the only S1 arm that does NOT render the registered CoT paragraph (Appendix F item 1). It is behaviourally equivalent to arm AS — same model, N, rounds, persona name, stance, temperature and resolved max_tokens bucket — differing only in that AS omits `effort` while this arm sets it explicitly to high, which the API documents as identical behaviour. That makes the documented equivalence itself observable rather than merely assumed: if this arm and a later arm-AS cell diverge beyond replicate noise, the equivalence claim is what to doubt.

uniformPersona.stance: No particular perspective is assigned for this task. Approach the brief however you judge best.

S1B-SOLO60.label: Study 1 Stage 1b — solo comparator, N=60
S1B-SOLO60.purpose: Appendix I item 2. The benchmark a panel must clear. Configured identically to S1-N60 (same model, N, effort, persona bundle) because it IS that condition re-collected: adding the Stage 1b arms moves armsConfigHash, which moves configHash, which stales every S1-* cell (Appendix D item 1). Stage 1a's ~49.4 distinct ideas from one call is the number this arm re-measures under the new hash, so panel-vs-solo is a within-run contrast rather than a comparison across two hashes.

uniformPersona.stance: No particular perspective is assigned for this task. Approach the brief however you judge best.

S1B-PANEL.label: Study 1 Stage 1b — panel, differentiated stances
S1B-PANEL.purpose: Appendix I item 2. The first panel this study has ever run. Default geometry (5 agents x ideasPerAgent 6 x maxRounds 2, blind then pool) gives a ~60-idea pool, matched to S1B-SOLO60 by construction. Model held at claude-sonnet-5 across every slot so the contrast is process, not model. Personas are DIFFERENTIATED -- but by stance and strategy only, never temperature (§3.3 strips sampling parameters universally), which is less differentiation than shipped DEFAULT_PERSONAS carries; Appendix I item 6 registers that as a stated limitation on any null result rather than a thing to change. Note also that these five slots fall through to DEFAULT_PERSONAS, four of which carry strategy 'cot' and one ('pragmatist') 'direct', so this arm differs from S1B-APRIME's uniform 'cot' bundle in one slot's strategy as well as in stance -- deliberately left as it ships, with the confound bounded by Stage 1a's own direct-vs-cot estimate (-0.58 [-2.14, 0.97]) and registered in Appendix I item 6.

S1B-APRIME.label: Study 1 Stage 1b — panel ablation, identical personas
S1B-APRIME.purpose: Appendix I item 2. Arm A' 's construction at Stage 1b's model and geometry: five identical agents under one explicit neutral persona, so it differs from S1B-PANEL in the persona lever and NOTHING else. This is what separates 'the personas did it' from 'we sampled five times' -- without it, a panel-beats-solo result cannot distinguish the product's claim from repeated sampling. The uniform persona is Stage 1a's own neutral bundle (solo_b), whose strategy 'cot' is also S1B-PANEL's MODAL value (4 of the 5 DEFAULT_PERSONAS), so the ablation is directly comparable to the solo arm's persona and differs from the panel's strategy in only one slot of five.

S1C-SOLO60.label: Study 1 Stage 1c -- solo comparator, N=60
S1C-SOLO60.purpose: Appendix L item 1. The benchmark, and the CROSS-RUN BRIDGE. Byte-identical in what it sends to S1B-SOLO60; only the hash label differs, because adding the S1C arms moves armsConfigHash and therefore stales every S1B cell (Appendix D item 1). The thin S1B-PANEL is deliberately NOT re-run, so a RICH-vs-PANEL comparison would cross a configHash boundary -- forbidden as a primary. This arm is what makes a SECONDARY one defensible: Appendix L item 4 registers that if this arm's rarefied mean reproduces Stage 1b's 44.570 within its CI and the rarefaction floors match, the cross-run comparison is reportable as clearly-labelled secondary, and if it does not reproduce, that claim is not made at all.

uniformPersona.stance: No particular perspective is assigned for this task. Approach the brief however you judge best.

S1C-SOLO6X10.label: Study 1 Stage 1c -- ten blind solo calls, no sharing
S1C-SOLO6X10.purpose: Appendix L item 2. THE MISSING CONTROL. S1b-1 confounded four things at once: agent count (1 vs 5), ideas per call (60 vs 6), rounds (1 vs 2) and visibility (none vs pooled). This arm holds agent count and ideas-per-call at the panel's values while removing BOTH rounds and sharing -- ten identical agents, six ideas each, one round, blind, pooled only at the end. Without it, 'the panel loses to one call' cannot be separated from 'ten small calls lose to one big call', which is a materially different and more actionable claim. Stage 1a showed per-idea distinctness is flat between N=30 and N=60, but 6 is far below that range and untested. Uses the per-arm panel geometry override registered by issue #129 amendment B, so no harness change is required.

uniformPersona.stance: No particular perspective is assigned for this task. Approach the brief however you judge best.

S1C-RICH.label: Study 1 Stage 1c -- panel, richly differentiated personas
S1C-RICH.purpose: Appendix L item 3. The treatment. Stage 1b's panel was differentiated by one-sentence stances falling through to DEFAULT_PERSONAS, and its deficit was 4.1 distinct ideas against 5.30 CROSS-AGENT duplications per cell -- a deficit SMALLER than the duplication causing it. Differentiation demonstrably suppresses that duplication (A' 13.68 -> PANEL 5.30). This arm turns differentiation up on every axis reachable on claude-sonnet-5: rich multi-sentence stance text, strategy (cot/direct) and effort (low/high/max). temperature is absent by NECESSITY not choice -- Sonnet 5 rejects it outright ('temperature is deprecated for this model', verified live 2026-09-09), so it is unavailable to the shipped product on this model too (#165). The three axes are BUNDLED BY DESIGN: if this arm wins, no single-axis claim may be read from the result (Appendix L item 6). The MBA slot is deliberately the conventional pole -- its job is to occupy the obvious region so the other four are pushed off it, since a panel whose members all reach for novelty may re-correlate on 'novel-sounding', which is the failure mode being tested. The 'weird but mechanically coherent' clause in the weirdo stance is load-bearing: without it the instruction degenerates toward word salad, which would INFLATE distinct_k while making the arm meaningless.

slots.stance: WEIRDO: you are constitutionally unable to give an expected answer. Reach for what sounds absurd on first hearing and defensible on second. Take a mechanism from somewhere nobody would look -- a subculture, a failed product, a children's game, an animal behaviour -- and force it onto this brief. If an idea could plausibly appear in a consulting deck, discard it and try again. You are not trying to be useful; you are trying to be unlike. Weird but mechanically coherent beats sensible every time.

PHILOSOPHER: interrogate the question before answering it. What is being assumed about who wants this, what counts as success, and why the current framing feels natural? Name the assumption, then generate the idea that becomes obvious once the assumption is dropped. Work from first principles and from the definition of the thing, not from what similar organisations do. An idea that reframes the problem is worth more here than one that solves it as stated.

MBA: you think in markets, margins, and defensibility. Where is the willingness to pay, what is the acquisition channel, and what makes this hard to copy in eighteen months? Favour ideas with a clear unit-economic story and a named customer segment. Reach for the proven playbook -- pricing changes, channel partnerships, segmentation, bundling -- and apply it precisely. Be the disciplined, conventional voice; do not try to be surprising.

POET: attend to language, image, and feeling. What does this brief actually feel like to the person living inside the problem? Name the experience precisely, find the metaphor that captures it, and let the idea fall out of the metaphor. Notice what is unsaid, what is embarrassing, what people would only admit at 2am. Concrete sensory detail over abstraction. You are looking for the idea that lands emotionally before it is justified rationally.

PRODUCT-MANAGER: a senior product management specialist. Think in terms of the user's job-to-be-done, the activation and retention loop, and the smallest testable slice. Apply craft knowledge: what actually moves adoption, where teams reliably fool themselves, which discovery method answers which uncertainty. Cite the mechanism -- why this changes behaviour -- not just the tactic. Prefer ideas you could put in front of five users next week and learn something falsifiable from.
